title.en: Explain the Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status

say.en: Before 1991 the government ran airlines, hotels, bakeries and even watch factories. Should it? Privatisation asks that question. In this lesson: Define privatisation and disinvestment.
Explain the Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status.
State the purpose of privatisation.

body.en: *Privatisation* means shedding the ownership or management of a government-owned enterprise. It can be done by withdrawing the government from ownership and management, or by outright sale. Selling part of the equity of public sector enterprises to the public is called disinvestment. The aim was to improve financial discipline and modernisation and to attract private capital and managerial skill.
body.kn: ಸರ್ಕಾರಿ ಉದ್ಯಮದ ಒಡೆತನ ಅಥವಾ ನಿರ್ವಹಣೆಯನ್ನು ಬಿಟ್ಟುಕೊಡುವುದೇ ಖಾಸಗೀಕರಣ. ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕ ಉದ್ಯಮಗಳ ಷೇರುಗಳ ಒಂದು ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ಜನರಿಗೆ ಮಾರುವುದು ಬಂಡವಾಳ ಹಿಂತೆಗೆತ (ನಿರ್ಹೂಡಿಕೆ).

title.en: On the board: Disinvestment in numbers

caption.en: A public sector company has 100 crore shares. The government sells part of its equity to the public. While it keeps at least 51% the firm is still a government company; below that, ownership has passed to private hands. A strategic sale also hands over management.

problem.en: The government owns 100% of a PSU with 10 crore shares. It sells 2.5 crore shares to the public at ₹80 each. What share does the government keep, and how much does it raise?

steps.en: Shares sold = 2.5 ÷ 10 = 25%, so the government keeps 75%.
Because the government keeps majority ownership, this is disinvestment, not full privatisation.

answer.en: Government keeps 75%; ₹200 crore raised through disinvestment.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. The government owns 100% of a PSU with 10 crore shares. It sells 2.5 crore shares to the public at ₹80 each. What share does the government keep, and how much does it raise?

say.en: Let us work through this together. The government owns 100 percent of a PSU with 10 crore shares. It sells 2.5 crore shares to the public at 80 rupees each. What share does the government keep, and how much does it raise?
Shares sold equals 2.5 divided by 10 equals 25 percent, so the government keeps 75 percent.
Money raised equals 2.5 crore times 80 rupees equals 200 rupees crore.
Because the government keeps majority ownership, this is disinvestment, not full privatisation.
So the answer is Government keeps 75 percent; 200 rupees crore raised through disinvestment.
